audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Renekton levels 4-5, first item and 2+ items and gave Skill to level 6, while the whys say levels 4-5 are where 'the lane levels out', level 6 is where Feast 'deters his dive', first item is 'force the fight here', and two items is 'the lane stays even'. The difficulty label is also wrong: HARD at 8.5/10 on a 49.77% win rate over 430 games, when the matchup's own late-game text says 'the reason this stays EVEN overall'.
audit.why: Renekton has no item scaling; Cho'Gath has Feast. His entire claim on the lane is levels 1-3 at 50 Fury.
audit.corrected: Renekton / Renekton / Renekton / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Skill — the packet chart — as one atomic group across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side+rating, plus diff EVEN and diffRating 6.5/10, with the difficulty and rating rows reworded to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase text named Heartsteel as the fight-forcing spike and listed 'levels 2-3 (full pattern)' as Cho'Gath's window, which is precisely Renekton's prime.
audit.why: Renekton's spikes are 50 Fury at levels 2-3 and Dominus at 6 (120s at rank 1); Cho'Gath's are level 6 and the first tank component. Renekton has nothing after that.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the matchup never names a single Renekton ability. Both layers say 'his empowered W', 'his E dash', 'his fury combo'. Also missing: Ruthless Predator is an auto-attack reset, so the tell is his auto wind-up rather than the cast; the empowered stun is 1.5s against 0.75s unempowered; and Dominus grants bonus health, which does nothing against Feast because Feast is true damage.
audit.why: A player reading 'his empowered W' cannot count the cooldown or recognise the wind-up. Ruthless Predator is 16s at rank 1 — the longest early cooldown either champion has — and that number is the whole basis for when Cho'Gath is allowed to step up.
audit.corrected: Cull the Meek, Ruthless Predator, Slice and Dice and Dominus named with their cooldowns across phases, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull, report[5].t and four content fields; the auto-reset tell added to dosFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was placeholder text with no numbers.
audit.why: Ruthless Predator 16s and Slice and Dice 16s at rank 1 are both long; Cull the Meek is a flat 7s and never off cooldown, which is why the punish window is defined by the other two.
audit.corrected: All three written in plus Dominus at 120s.

audit.why: Cull the Meek heals off every swing and the heal scales at 50 Fury, so early Grievous Wounds and armour are right — report[8].t already says both. Recorded rather than changed.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Identify how Renekton contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: A level-1 bully with Cull the Meek healing off every swing and no sustain edge on your side — start Q, give ground, do not contest CS.

edits.before: W silence starts flipping his combo windows. Only take the trade when Renekton's Ruthless Predator is down.
edits.after: At 50 Fury Ruthless Predator stuns for 1.5s instead of 0.75s and opens the all-in before your Rupture.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Renekton must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Slice and Dice in, the Fury combo, Slice and Dice back out — all of it before a telegraphed Rupture ever lands.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Ruthless Predator's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Carnivore sustain, Vorpal Spikes waveclear and the Rupture-into-Feral-Scream combo finally answer him as his early prime ends.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Renekton's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast is true damage, so neither his armour nor Dominus's bonus health saves him — land Rupture into Feral Scream and threaten the kill on an empty Fury bar.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Ruthless Predator's cooldown.
edits.after: A tank component plus Feast stacks let you eat the Fury combo and silence off his escape dash.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Renekton carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He has no item scaling while you keep stacking Feast, but his low cooldowns let him splitpush and flank-dive instead of dueling.

edits.before: Q under Renekton's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Rupture him once Slice and Dice is spent, Feral Scream so the second dash cannot answer, then E-spike your way out.

edits.before: Whiffing Q and fighting anyway — without the knockup your kit is a slow zone with no teeth.
edits.after: Trading at 50 Fury — Ruthless Predator stuns 1.5s and the combo lands before your Q.

edits.before: Empowered = long stun. Silence it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 16s at rank 1 — his longest early cooldown. Step up once it is spent.

edits.before: Q under Renekton's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Ruthless Predator is an auto-attack reset, so his auto wind-up is the tell, not the cast — Rupture on the wind-up.

edits.before: Renekton wastes Ruthless Predator (Stun) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Cull the Meek is a flat 7s and heals him — Grievous Wounds early matters.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: At 50 Fury the stun doubles to 1.5 seconds. Watch the Fury bar.

edits.before: - Renekton Ruthless Predator: matchup-defining — Empowered = long stun. Silence it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Ruthless Predator: 16s at rank 1, his longest early cooldown and the whole all-in; at 50 Fury it stuns 1.5s instead of 0.75s. - Slice and Dice: 16s at rank 1, in and out. - Dominus: 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Respect Renekton's Ruthless Predator completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Last-hit at max range, lean on Carnivore, and concede CS rather than HP. Your one safe window is his second Slice and Dice: once he has dashed in and the stun is spent, Rupture into Feral Scream.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 8.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Ruthless Predator and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6.5/10. The lane is decided by whether you reach level 6 with enough health for Feast to matter.

edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 6.5/10, Renekton carry threat 8.5/10.

edits.after: Ruthless Predator is 16s at rank 1 and stuns 1.5s at 50 Fury; Feast's true damage beats Dominus's bonus health.

notes: Renekton's empowered Ruthless Predator 'destroy[s] damage shields on the target' per Riot's text. Cho'Gath has no shield in his kit, so I deliberately said nothing about it rather than write a non-interaction — but it is worth knowing if the player runs a shielding rune or item. NOT ASSERTED: whether Ruthless Predator's stun is reduced by tenacity, whether Feral Scream's silence can prevent the Slice and Dice recast specifically (the text claims it 'denies his escape dash', which I left alone but did not strengthen), and whether Dominus's bonus health counts toward Feast's execute threshold — Feast's kit carries a percentHealth flag but the threshold mechanics are not in Riot's description, so I wrote only that Dominus's health does not stop true damage.
